text:
sam_sales: GyroShip POC — customer hit a blocker with our Rust WS client and structured tool-calls. They need clarification on binary frames, per-message trace_id, telemetry hooks, and SOC2/data retention. Can eng + legal weigh in?

alex_engineer: We support both text and binary WS frames. Our Rust sample uses tokio-tungstenite. Quick snippet:```rust
let (mut ws_stream, _) = connect_async(url).await?;
ws_stream.send(Message::Binary(payload)).await?;
```For structured tool calls we wrap the payload in a JSON envelope (tool:..., args:...). trace_id can be supplied either as an HTTP header during the initial handshake (X-Trace-Id) or as a top-level field in the envelope.

maria_se: Customer specifically asked about ack semantics and commit callbacks (they want at-least-once guarantees for downstream processing). By default our streaming is best-effort — do we have an ack mode for POC?

alex_engineer: Ack mode exists today in Dedicated/Private runtimes (not enabled for Hosted by default). It can be enabled via query params on the handshake. Expect extra latency: ~40-120ms per-message depending on batch and seq len. Example handshake:```http
GET /v1/stream?client=rust&ack=true&proto=json HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```The Rust client toggles ack in the URL and listens for server ACK events. We also provide a dedupe token you can include to avoid double-processing.

alex_engineer: Also note binary frames are recommended for large proto payloads to reduce overhead; JSON envelope preferred for readable tool-calls.

maria_se: From a presales perspective: they want telemetry for compliance — connection lifecycle, per-request latency histograms, sample traces, and a sampling rate control. Can we surface those to the customer for POC?

alex_engineer: Yes. We can expose a telemetry hook for POC with these fields: connection_id, trace_id, sample_rate, event_type, latency_ms, and an optional user_id (redacted if PII). We'll also add aggregated histograms (p50/p95/p99). For security we can mask token-level payloads. I'll add the hook to the runbook.

jess_legal: SOC2/legal asks: how long are raw requests/responses retained for Hosted POC? Are model inputs used for training? They also want a template SOC2 attestation and confirmation on IP allowlist + SAML SSO support.

alex_engineer: Hosted POC: raw request/response logs are retained 30 days by default for debugging; we can shorten to 7/14/30 or disable retention for Dedicated/Private. We do not use customer PII or model inputs for training per the standard enterprise contract. For SSO, Hosted supports SAML SSO + enterprise SSO integrations and IP allowlisting on the account.

sam_sales: Pricing Q — customer asked: "if we run 10k concurrent WS connections with ~100 req/s each, what do we recommend?" (they're unsure about tokens per request).

maria_se: Clarify numbers — 10k * 100 r/s = 1M r/s which is extremely large. If that's accurate, recommend Dedicated reserved GPU fleet and architecture review. For most POCs customers mean 10k connections with occasional bursts, not sustained 100 r/s per connection. For POC: propose a small reserved pool with burst + on-demand fallback. I'll draft a cost sketch but need expected tokens per request.

alex_engineer: Action items for POC: 1) I'll push a minimal Rust sample (handshake + binary frames + ack fallback) to the runbook. 2) Add telemetry example and how to set sample_rate. 3) Document perf hit when ack=true.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Runbook created -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gyroship-1768620000. CI job created: #build-gyroship-rust-sample-176862.

jess_legal: I'll attach SOC2 summary + fill the questionnaire. Also confirm we can provide a temporary Data Processing Addendum (DPA) for the POC with retention controls.

sam_sales: Great. Next steps: Alex drop rust sample + handshake details in runbook, Maria push initial pricing sketch (assume 2k conn baseline), Jess attach SOC2 + DPA. I'll sync with the customer tomorrow morning.

alex_engineer: Quick note — edge-case: corp proxies sometimes rewrite WS headers causing X-Trace-Id drop. Recommend adding trace_id inside the JSON envelope as fallback.

maria_se: +1. Also ask the customer about expected token sizes (avg tokens/request) and whether they will use tool-calls that return large payloads (docs, embeddings).

sam_sales: 👍 thanks everyone — I'll update thread after the customer call.
